title: Margenau-Hill distribution as a Necessary and Sufficient Signature of Measurement Incompatibility
abstract: Measurement incompatibility and the negativity of quasi-probability distributions both demonstrate the signature of nonclassicality. However, their relations largely remained qualitative, and no explicit operational connection has been established. We provide an operational link between measurement incompatibility and the Margenau-Hill(MH) quasi-probability distribution associated with two dichotomic observables. { We first derive the joint measurability (measurement compatibility) condition for any pair of dichotomic observables in arbitrary finite dimension $d$.} We then rigorously prove that for any pair of unsharp dichotomic measurements in dimension $d$, the positivity of the MH distribution is equivalent to joint measurability \emph{i.e.}, the MH distribution is positive \emph{if and only if} the measurements are jointly measurable. We further introduce the MH-like quasi-probability distribution for $n$ dichotomic unsharp observables in arbitrary finite dimension and derive a sufficient condition of joint-measurability when the observables are mutually anticommuting. Finally, we propose an interferometric setup, inspired by quantum-switch architectures, that directly reconstructs MH quasi-probability which in turn provides a test of incompatibility.
summary: This paper establishes that the positivity of the Margenau-Hill quasi-probability distribution serves as a necessary and sufficient condition for two unsharp quantum measurements to be jointly measurable. The authors derive the mathematical criteria and propose an experimental protocol using an interferometer to directly measure this distribution, providing a powerful test for quantum incompatibility.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a rigorous, operational link between the concept of measurement incompatibility and the mathematical positivity of the Margenau-Hill (MH) quasi-probability distribution for dichotomic observables.
main_result: It is proven that for unsharp dichotomic measurements, the positivity of the MH distribution is necessary and sufficient for the measurements to be jointly measurable (i.e., compatible).
method: The authors derive joint measurability conditions by analyzing the positivity of the MH distribution, which is then experimentally tested using a modified Mach-Zehnder interferometer setup.
model_or_system: The study focuses on general quantum systems described by density matrices, specifically analyzing pairs (and generalizations to $n$) of dichotomic observables in an arbitrary finite dimension $d$.
key_observables: The Margenau-Hill (MH) quasi-probability distribution, $q(a_1, a_2)$, and the expectation value $\langle P_\Psi angle$ measured in an interferometer.
important_parameters: The dimension of the Hilbert space ($d$), and the parameters ($\lambda, \mu$) defining the unsharpness of the measurements.
main_assumptions: The equivalence between MH positivity and joint measurability is rigorously proven for two dichotomic unsharp observables; the generalization to $n$ observables relies on the assumption that they are mutually anticommuting.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the interferometric setup, inspired by quantum-switch architectures, designed to directly measure the MH quasi-probability distribution.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the general joint measurability condition for two observables, then proves the equivalence between MH positivity and joint measurability, generalizes this to $n$ observables, and concludes by detailing the experimental realization of the test using interferometry.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally testable diagnostic tool (the MH distribution) to quantify quantum incompatibility, bridging abstract mathematical concepts with physical measurement limitations.
